question: Due to presence of which particle, does Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER) look rough under a microscope?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ribosome**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)** appears rough under a microscope due to the presence of **ribosomes** attached to its surface.
 
• Ribosomes are responsible for **protein synthesis**, a critical cellular function essential for growth, repair, and maintaining cellular processes.
 
• The RER is primarily involved in the **synthesis of proteins** that are either secreted by the cell, incorporated into the cell membrane, or sent to lysosomes.
 
• These ribosomes are bound to the cytosolic surface of the RER and help in translating messenger RNA (mRNA) into polypeptide chains.
